agents.task: Test authentication and JWT vulnerabilities on OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on token validation, token forgery, user enumeration, and weak password reset. Test JWT algorithm confusion, unsigned tokens, weak secrets, and token reuse. Probe the registration and login flows for bypasses. If vulnerabilities found, spawn validation agents for working PoCs.

Test business logic vulnerabilities on OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on price manipulation, negative quantity abuse, coupon/discount bypass, order workflow manipulation, and payment flow abuse. Test race conditions on concurrent operations. If vulnerabilities found, spawn validation agents for working PoCs and impact demonstration.

Test IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) and authorization bypass vulnerabilities on OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on user-specific endpoints (/api/Users, /api/Orders, /api/Cards, /api/BasketItems, /api/Complaints). Enumerate object IDs and test if users can access other users' data without proper authorization. Test both horizontal (same-level) and vertical (privilege escalation) access control bypass. If vulnerabilities found, spawn validation agents for working PoCs.

Validate and report the IDOR vulnerability in user modification on OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. The vulnerability allows a customer user to modify any other user's profile (email, password) via PUT /api/Users/{target_id}. Create detailed PoC showing: 1) Customer user forges unsigned token 2) Modifies admin user (ID 1) data 3) Verifies changes persisted. Test authorization bypass across user IDs. File create_vulnerability_report with CVSS scoring (confidentiality+integrity impact). No source code fixing required (black-box app).

Validate and report the unsigned JWT token (alg=none) vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. Create a detailed working PoC demonstrating complete authentication bypass - forge tokens for different users, access admin endpoints, modify user data. File create_vulnerability_report with full technical details, CVSS scoring, and code locations if source available. Test across /api/Users/{id}, /api/Orders, /api/Cards, /api/Complaints endpoints.

Validate and report the SQL injection vulnerability in the login endpoint of OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. The /rest/user/login endpoint is vulnerable to SQL injection - payload: {\"email\": \"' OR 1=1 --\", \"password\": \"anything\"} returns 200 with admin token. Demonstrate: 1) Bypass authentication without credentials 2) Gain admin access 3) Create detailed PoC. File create_vulnerability_report with CVSS (authentication bypass, data access).

Perform complete reconnaissance on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Map the entire attack surface: all endpoints, parameters, forms, technologies, authentication model, user roles, and capabilities. Document all discovered APIs, endpoints, and features. Produce a comprehensive inventory of the application's structure and reachable surfaces. This will inform threat modeling and guide targeted vulnerability testing by specialized agents.

Test SQL injection vulnerabilities on the OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on the /api/Products/search endpoint and any other endpoints accepting user input that may reach database queries. Test with classic SQLi payloads, time-based blind SQLi, error-based SQLi, and UNION-based extraction. If SQLi is found, spawn a validation agent to build a working PoC and confirm exploitability. Document all findings with exact endpoint, parameter, and payload.

Validate and build a working proof-of-concept for SQL injection vulnerability in OWASP Juice Shop /rest/products/search endpoint. The endpoint is confirmed vulnerable with the parameter 'q' (GET). SQL injection is confirmed via boolean-based SQLi (query manipulation affects response size). Build a complete PoC demonstrating: 1) Boolean-based blind SQLi to extract database information, 2) Data extraction from tables, 3) Exact payload that demonstrates exploitability. Target: http://host.docker.internal:3100

Test Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities on OWASP Juice Shop at http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on public endpoints like /api/Feedbacks, /api/SecurityQuestions, and any user input that gets reflected or stored. Test for reflected XSS, stored XSS, and DOM-based XSS. Use browser automation to verify script execution. If vulnerabilities found, spawn validation agents for working PoCs and impact demonstration.

entries.evidence: Application accepts JWT tokens with alg=none and no signature. Tested with /api/Users/1 returning 200 with user data. Allows forging tokens for any user with any claims."

Customer with token for User 2 can modify User 1 email/password. PUT /api/Users/1 with different user's token returns 200. All users 1-4 modified successfully. No authorization check on user_id parameter."
Payload injected into DOM: is reflected in searchValue span element without sanitization

API endpoint /api/BasketItems returns 500 errors with "WHERE parameter ProductId has invalid undefined value". Could not fully test negative quantity abuse due to API contract issues. The API appears to expect a specific request format not yet reverse-engineered from working traffic. This requires either source code inspection or capturing actual browser-generated requests to understand the correct payload structure.

entries.risk_area: Business Logic - Order State Machine Bypass
entries.evidence: POST /api/Orders endpoint returns 500 errors. Could not validate whether order state transitions are enforced or whether workflow steps can be bypassed. Requires correct API contract format to test properly.

GET /api/BasketItems/coupon returns 404, POST returns 500. Coupon endpoint structure unclear. OWASP Juice Shop is known to have discount-related vulnerabilities, but could not validate without proper API understanding. Known OWASP Juice Shop coupon codes (OWASP2017, etc.) were not testable due to API format issues.

Products endpoint returns correctly formatted product data with server-defined prices (price: 1.99, deluxePrice: 0.99). The API returns these values to the client, but business logic testing of whether client-submitted prices are accepted in basket operations could not be completed due to BasketItems endpoint failures. However, the product prices are clearly server-sourced and would need to be re-validated server-side on order creation (standard e-commerce practice).

entries.risk_area: Business Logic + Authorization - IDOR on Baskets
entries.evidence: GET /api/Baskets/{id} returns 500 errors. OWASP Juice Shop is known to have IDOR vulnerabilities. Could not test whether one user can access another user's basket without proper API contract. Requires source code review or browser-based testing to confirm.

Confirmed horizontal IDOR: authenticated user can access any other user's profile data via /api/Users/{userId} endpoint. Working PoC demonstrates attacker accessing victim's email, role, and personal metadata without authorization.
